A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Target-Aware Video Diffusion Models work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation comparisons, two user studies, ablations, qualitative demonstrations and physics-based imitation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds mask and caption robustness experiments, stricter interaction measurements, domain-transfer demonstrations and failure cases.

M1.justification: The core mask-channel architecture, target token, attention loss and LoRA training remain. v3 adds an automated GPT-4o/Grounded-SAM mask-acquisition pipeline and an egocentric adaptation procedure that transfers the target-aware LoRA onto a separately fine-tuned backbone (Appendices B and C.1).

E1.justification: The 1,290-clip BEHAVE/Ego-Exo4D training collection remains. v3 adds EgoIT-99 training for egocentric generation, explicit outdoor human-interaction tests, corrupted or automatically generated conditioning inputs, and multiple-object and temporal target-switching scenarios. These substantially broaden viewpoint, environment and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: The CogVideoX, data-fine-tuned CogVideoX and adapted Direct-a-video attention-modulation baselines remain, as do DragDiffusion, Go-with-the-Flow and inpainting comparisons. The CogVideoX-Ego experiment extends the existing backbone-versus-target-aware comparison through domain fine-tuning; it does not introduce a distinct competing method.

E3.justification: The principal benchmark grows from 50 to 80 images, yielding 250 versus 400 videos. v3 introduces stricter temporal/contact-plus-motion metrics, 50-image mask experiments, egocentric adaptation and additional ablation settings. Its Section 4.3 specifies every fifth supervised block, conflicting with Appendix A.1's retained every-third setting; the actual block schedule therefore remains unresolved.

E4.justification: v3 adds mask dilation, erosion, circular-mask and automatic-segmentation tests; caption-removal training ablations and corrupted-prompt inference tests; and explicit multiple-object and target-switching failures. It also expands loss-weight sensitivity and domain-transfer/action-diversity analyses. The original block-selection, attention-region and attention-modulation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies that the five videos per test image use random seeds; v1 already reported five videos per image. This adds seed information without establishing increased repetition. Neither version supplies confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original ablation tables contain revised scores: the proposed method's Contact Score changes from 0.896 to 0.878, and data-fine-tuned CogVideoX changes from 0.692 to 0.638. These concern different benchmark sizes, not demonstrated same-setting declines. New Table 9 reports 0.770, 0.693 and 0.783 for the proposed method's two-frame, three-frame and Interaction Scores. Numerous robustness and qualitative findings are added; user-study scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces precise definitions for consecutive-frame Contact Score and Interaction Score, which combines contact with a target-displacement threshold. The diffusion objectives and attention equations remain substantively equivalent; the downsampled-mask notation is clarified. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 retains the central target-aware generation, curated-dataset and two-application contributions. It reframes the loss contribution from proposing a novel cross-attention loss to utilizing cross-attention supervision, and adds an explicit introductory claim of robustness to mask quality. Motion-planning motivation receives greater emphasis but already existed in v1.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking noisy captions to preservation of pretrained priors and grounding to the target token rather than the object noun. It identifies channel-scaling, multi-object-mask and temporal-switching limitations, and explains the hand detector's inapplicability to non-human agents. Appendix C.3 also discusses false positives and undercounting under the original and extended metrics.

D1.justification: Most training and inference details are retained. v3 adds parameter-count and VRAM-saving information, evaluation-mask selection instructions, automatic-mask hardware/timing details and more precise inference timing. It adds a project-page pointer while omitting v1's future code/data-release statement; the PDFs do not establish actual release availability.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly connects the planning motivation to World Models, Navigation World Models and Dexterous World Models, and adds references supporting new components, including Grounded-SAM, CoTracker and EgoLife. The established controllable-video and human-scene positioning remains. Publication-year and venue updates to retained works do not constitute additional research.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around target awareness and motion planning. Application order is reversed, the video-creation account is condensed, attention-region and block discussions are reordered, and the main discussion becomes a conclusion. The appendix is reorganized into thematic discussions, including relocated and expanded limitations.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. The opening teaser is removed, method diagrams and attention visualizations are merged into paired figures, and the video-creation pipeline moves to the appendix. New robustness tables and extensive qualitative and failure-case figures substantially change the visual presentation beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the central claim. Unlike v1, it tests dependence on mask precision and caption quality, checks whether the advantage survives stricter temporal/contact-plus-motion criteria, and documents concrete failure boundaries (Tables 5–9 and Appendix C). These address important weaknesses in v1's reliance on single-frame contact and limited robustness evidence. The new block-selection inconsistency harms reproducibility, and statistical uncertainty remains unreported, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidential depth and qualification.
